text:
TCU women's golf team holds third after first round in Japan tournament
Three members of the TCU women's golf team placed within the top 10 on the individual leaderboard, helping TCU secure third place after 18 holes at the Pan Pacific University Golf Super League tournament in Shizuoka, Japan, on Sep. 2.
TCU finished four strokes over par with a score of 288 during round one at Grand Fields Country Club in Mishima. The team trails San Jose State by one shot for second place and is ahead of other Division I teams including Long Beach State and Florida Gulf Coast. The tournament features a field of 12 teams, including five Japanese universities as well as squads from Europe, South Korea, and Taiwan. Nihon University leads with a score of 13-under-par 271.
The event marks TCU's first competition in Asia. Junior transfer Claire Swathwood led TCU on day one with a one-under-par round of 70, placing her fourth individually. Swathwood recorded five birdies and achieved her eleventh career par-or-better round. Yvette O'Brien scored even par to tie for fifth place, while Gracie McGovern shot a 72 to finish tied for tenth.
O'Brien has finished even par in three out of her last four rounds dating back to April's Big 12 Championship. She matched Swathwood’s birdie total and was added to the lineup due to Kirstin Angosta's illness. Camille Min-Gaultier and Ella Forss each completed their opening rounds at four-over-par, tying for twenty-fourth place.
The Horned Frogs began strong on the front nine with Swathwood, O'Brien, and McGovern all entering the turn at one-under as part of a collective three-under-par effort (141). However, they picked up seven strokes on the tougher back nine; O'Brien closed her round with consecutive birdies on holes seventeen and eighteen.
TCU will begin second-round play at approximately 6:40 p.m. Central Time Wednesday evening. There is no live scoring available; results will be finalized after play concludes.
